title: Disaster Related Extension of Deadlines Act

claims.claim: When the IRS postpones tax deadlines because of a disaster

claims.note: Postponement authority is section 7508A ('by reason of disasters'); IRS is the standard administrator of 7508A, not named verbatim in this enacted text.

claims.claim: this makes that extra time also count toward the deadline for claiming a tax refund

claims.claim: The new 6303(b)(2) applies to any period disregarded under 7508A — which by its own heading covers 'significant fire, or terroristic or military actions' as well as disasters — but the analysis frames the scope narrowly as 'disaster-related' throughout
claims.sourceSpan: Postponement by reason of disaster, significant fire, or terroristic or military actions
claims.note: Minor scope-narrowing: the analysis says 'disaster' everywhere, but the operative paragraph (and 7508A generally) also covers significant fire and terroristic/military postponements. The bill's official title, short title, and Sec. 2 heading all frame it as 'by reason of disasters', so the plain-English gloss is defensible; noted as visible scope debt, not material.

notes: Source = enacted Public Law 119-64 text (2476 chars, read in full). Two IRC amendments only: (a) adds 7508A(f) making any 7508A-disregarded filing period an extension of time for filing for purposes of the 6511(b)(2)(A) refund/credit limitation, effective for claims filed after enactment; (b) restructures 6303(b) into (1)/(2) and adds (2) so the last date for payment on a collection notice accounts for any 7508A-disregarded period, effective for notices issued after enactment.
